title: When to plant okra
seoTitle: When to Plant Okra: Soil Temperature and Dates by Zone

intro: Okra loves heat. Plant it into cold ground and the seed sits and rots, but wait for warm soil and it comes up fast and grows all summer.
Need seeds? Start with [free okra seeds](/okra/free-okra-seeds) from Olivia's garden.

blocks.text: Texas A&M AgriLife recommends planting okra [2 to 3 weeks after all danger of frost has passed](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/). The soil matters more than the calendar, though. Okra seed needs soil of [at least 65°F at a depth of 4 inches](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), and it sprouts best between 70°F and 95°F.

blocks.title: Check the soil, not the date
blocks.text: Push a soil thermometer 4 inches into the bed in the morning. When it reads 65°F or warmer, it's time to plant.

sections.title: When to plant okra in your zone

blocks.text: Enter your ZIP code to find your USDA hardiness zone and the usual spring planting window there. Zones are based on winter cold, not frost dates, so treat the window as a starting point and let your soil temperature make the final call.

sections.title: When to plant okra in North Texas

blocks.text: In McKinney, which is zone 8b, we plant okra in mid April. The latest we've planted is the first few days of June, and those plants still gave us a good crop.

blocks.title: From Olivia's garden
blocks.text: We plant once a year. Our okra plants get big and keep producing pods all season, so there's no need for a second planting.

sections.title: What happens if you plant okra too early

blocks.text: In cold, wet soil, okra seed is slow to sprout and seedlings grow slowly. Clemson Extension notes that [root-decay diseases that kill young seedlings](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/) are the most serious okra problem, and they're more common when okra goes into cold, wet soil.

sections.title: Starting okra indoors in short-season areas

blocks.text: Where summers are short, give okra a head start inside. University of Minnesota Extension suggests [starting okra indoors in mid March](https://extension.umn.edu/garden-and-home/yard-and-garden/gardening-in-minnesota/starting-seeds-indoors) and keeping the plants inside about 9 weeks, until after the last frost.

Okra doesn't like having its roots disturbed, so sow each seed in its own pot and plant it out without breaking up the root ball. Okra takes about [55 to 65 days from planting to first harvest](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/texas-home-vegetable-gardening-guide/), so check that your summer is long enough.

sections.title: Do you need a second planting?

blocks.text: Usually not. One spring planting keeps producing all season. If you're getting a late start or want a separate fall crop, AgriLife recommends planting [at least 3 months before the first fall frost](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/). Count back 3 months from your usual first frost to find your last planting date.

You can also keep spring plants going instead of replanting. When production slows in the heat of mid to late summer, cutting the plants back makes them regrow. Clemson Extension calls this [ratooning](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), and the plants start producing again in about 4 to 6 weeks, until frost.

faq.question: What temperature should the soil be to plant okra?
faq.answer: At least 65°F at a depth of 4 inches, and 70°F or warmer is better. In colder soil, okra sprouts slowly and seedlings are more likely to rot.

faq.question: What's the latest you can plant okra?
faq.answer: Count back 3 months from your first fall frost. Plants need that long to grow and give you a harvest before cold weather stops them.

faq.question: Can you grow okra in Canada?
faq.answer: In the warmest areas, yes. Start seeds indoors, plant out after your last frost once the soil is warm, and choose a sunny, sheltered spot.
